items.title: dsh-superagent-prototype
items.description: Towards a More Autonomous Agent System
items.summary: DeepSeek just open-sourced dsh-superagent, a proactive coding agent built for a single GitHub repository. It listens to issues and pull requests, then runs many agents in parallel to clear work while demanding almost no ongoing human attention. The design follows one clear rule: take as little human attention as possible and deliver as much value as possible. The team notes that much of the engineering was done by coding agents themselves and that the code is intended for reference and adaptation, not as a production product. It sits alongside their broader Super-agent design that separates a long-running router from parallel worker sessions so one conversation can span multiple concurrent tasks without forcing people to track every session.

items.title: Mika
items.description: An on-device AI agent for Android that operates apps and the web to get things done for you.
items.summary: Mika is an on-device AI agent for Android that operates apps and the web to get things done for you. It is open-source and written in Cotlin, emphasizing privacy by working on your phone without relying on remote models or screenshot streaming. Mika can handle scheduled tasks, remember your preferences, and operates in a hidden background screen, allowing you to use your phone while it works. It uses your own AI model and runs scripts in a Linux sandbox, ensuring tasks are completed privately. The project has gained significant attention, with over 4,000 stars on GitHub.

items.title: agent-autoloop
items.description: 让你的命令行 Agent 在后台自己接活、自己跟进到底；平时不烦你，遇到拿不准的事才发卡片找你拍板。
items.summary: Agent-Autoloop is an open-source command line agent automation system that allows your agent to independently handle tasks in the background without bothering you unless it encounters uncertain situations, at which point it sends a card to you for decision-making. The system has been refined over a year and is designed to run autonomously, taking on tasks like cron jobs and GitHub issues, and it can interface with various agents like Claude code or Codex. It operates without external dependencies and integrates with platforms like Feishu, DingTalk, and Slack for notifications. The core of Agent-Autoloop is a lightweight, 1600-line code kernel with four mechanisms: suspending with zero consumption, event traceability, command-data separation, and jump number meltdown.

items.title: FlashProve
items.description: A research prototype for zero-knowledge proofs of AI inference. Not maintained.
items.summary: Anthropic released FlashProve, an open-source research prototype for zero-knowledge proofs of AI inference, on November 2, 2026. The system uses cryptographic proofs to verify AI model outputs without revealing the model weights. FlashProve generates proofs at 110 tokens per second for Meta’s 400-billion-parameter Llama 4 Maverick model on a single H100 GPU, with each proof sized at about 19 MB. The system is based on zero-knowledge succinct arguments of knowledge (zkSNARKs) and is described as an unmaintained research artifact. The FlashProve repository includes a prover, a fast C++ verifier, a slower Lean verifier, Lean proofs, and an interactive theorem visualizer under the Apache 2.0 license.

items.title: uni-robot-agent

items.summary: The uni-robot-agent is a unified and modular harness for robot use without privileged inputs, designed for generalizable agentic training. It unifies interaction records across environments and supports efficient experience collection for open models. The tool interfaces and feedback formats span models, robots, tasks, and environments, making simulation and real-world experience easier to combine for training.
